newsitem.title: GERMANY: CDU wants tax compromise with SPD by Easter - Hintze.
newsitem.headline: CDU wants tax compromise with SPD by Easter - Hintze.

text.p: Chancellor Helmut Kohl's Christian Democrats (CDU) on Monday urged opposition Social Democrats (SPD) to reach a compromise on crucial tax reforms by Easter on the basis of a coalition plan to shave 30 billion marks in tax.
Speaking just before Kohl was to lead a coalition team into a tax summit with SPD leader Oskar Lafontaine, CDU general secretary Peter Hintze said he was hopeful of early progress.

"By Easter we must have clarity over whether the SPD...is really ready to work with us on tax reforms or just revert to its blocking strategy," Hintze told reporters after a meeting of CDU leaders approved the party's negotiating position.
Party chiefs reaffirmed that a tax plan to cut income and corporate taxes worked out under Finance Minister Theo Waigel remained the only basis for coalition negotiators.
"The concept that we are bringing into these talks is the concept put together by (Waigel's) tax reform commission -- in all its elements," Hintze said.
Changes demanded by the SPD -- such as keeping tax relief for anti-social work hours -- would have to be thoroughly argued and financed if they were to be accepted, Hintze said.
And SPD calls to keep the top rate of personal income tax high, while cutting rates for the self-employed were "very questionable", Hintze added.
Although he said he was optimistic, Hintze said: "There will not be a reform at any price and we will not allow the reforms to be talked to death."

If the talks fail and the SPD blocks tax reforms in the upper house of parliament, Hintze said the government would fight for its policies in forthcoming regional elections, and, if necessary in the general election campaign of autumn 1998.
